reason: A shape word for a structure that narrows into a neck (an urn, capsule or fruit). The neck itself is just the narrowed top of that structure, so the word describes the bearer rather than naming a separate part.
A text-extraction error: 'peduncle', 'leaf' and 'flower' run together. The examples are about a leaf ('feuille supérieure réduite') and a petiole comparison. It is a fragment, not a part name.

target: pattern 10 (ratio to another part): second term stamen (PO_0009029)
reason: '1/3-1/2 as long as stamens' gives the length of another part (an appendage) compared with the stamens. The stamen is the thing compared against, not the bearer, and 'stamen length' is a quality of the stamen, not a part.
A taxon rank ('Varieties 2-4', '2 variétés'), not a plant part.
Exact: PO lists 'free ending vein' and 'freely ending vein' as synonyms. In 'sori on 1-8 vein endings' these are the free vein ends of a fern leaf.

target: trichome (PO_0000282), read as hairs arranged in a ring at the apex of the part being described (bearer = trichome, its position = apex of the whole)
reason: A ring or tuft of hairs at the top of an organ, such as a seed, ovary or fruit. It is a group of trichomes in one place, not a separate organ. Where it is the calyx of an Asteraceae fruit, pappus (PO_0025393) would be the better bearer, but that needs context.

target: plant ovule (PO_0020003), pattern 12, whole = flower (PO_0009046) with female (PATO_0000383); count by pattern 03
reason: The ovules of a female flower. The sex belongs to the flower (the whole), not to the ovule, which is the case pattern 12 covers. Narrower use of plant ovule.
A surface-texture word (with small pits or grooves). Its nearest PATO term is foveate (PATO_0002296). Here it was misread as a part; the 'fossules' are surface features of the bearer.
A raised ridge across the node joining the bases of opposite petioles, as in Rubiaceae and Loganiaceae. It is a ridge on the node, best read as the node being crested, not as a separate organ.
A quality word (nectar-producing). The parts in the examples already have classes: 'anneau nectarifère' is the floral disc (FLOPO_0986025), and 'fossette nectarifère' is a nectary (PO_0009035).
An arrangement quality: FLOPO:0991004 paired already exists. 'spine-pairs' is a spine (bearer) that is paired.

Narrower: a branched (panicle) inflorescence whose last branches are racemes. Compound raceme inflorescence (PO_0030116) is close, but floras use 'panicle' for the overall branching, so the panicle class is the safer parent.

Narrower: a cluster that looks like a fascicle but comes from a shortened cyme or short shoot. In floras it nearly always describes a flower cluster. Too rare and too close to fascicle to justify a class of its own.
A quality: vestigial (PATO_0000588). 'rudiments du sexe avorté' are vestigial organs of the other sex (a pistillode or staminode); the part is named elsewhere in the sentence.
A quality word (made of sclerenchyma). The tissue itself is sclerenchyma (PO_0005427), and the fibres are plant fiber cells (PO_0025407).
The plant's below-ground parts taken together (rhizome, tuber, roots), used when the flora does not say which. Read as a plant structure in the subterranean state, not a new class.
A position quality: FLOPO:0991036 aerial already exists. The part is the root or rootlet in the same phrase.
'aerial root' is already listed as a synonym of shoot-borne root in PO (synonym only, not an exact match).
Exact: French for septum (partition). In fruit or ovary contexts the narrower fruit septum (PO_0025268) or plant ovary septum (PO_0025262) applies. Septum is the safe common parent.
'en collerette' (collar-like) describes the shape of the bearer, for example 'Androcée en collerette' is the androecium (PO_0009061) forming a ring. It is not a separate part.
Generic part ('outgrowth'): it needs the organ it grows from. Treated like 'segment' and 'scale' in the previous review.

target: pistillate flower (PO_0025599) with basal position in the inflorescence (pattern 04)
reason: Female flowers placed at the base of the inflorescence: a position in a series, which pattern 04 expresses. The count ('0-1(2) fleur ♀') uses pattern 03.
A shape quality, filamentous (PATO_0001360). 'coronal filaments' are parts of the floral corona (FLOPO:0985020), which is the bearer.
Exact: French form of '-foliolate', which config/flora_counted_parts.tsv already maps to leaflet. '3-foliolées' means three leaflets.
Narrower: small gland spots (often see-through dots) on leaves or petals. Where they are oil cavities, oil gland (PO_0005669) is the narrower class.
An arrangement of the bearer: whorled (PATO_0001951), with a count of two whorls. The bearer is the stamens or perianth named in the sentence.
A substance: threads of latex seen when a leaf or branch is torn. It is not an anatomical structure, though laticifer cells (PO_0025031) are what produce the latex.
A generic surface feature: it needs the organ it is on. Treated like 'rib' in the previous review. The quality reading is grooved (PATO_0002255) on that organ.
A colour patch on a petal, lip or leaf, which is a colour-pattern quality of the bearer (blotchy PATO_0000329 or spotted PATO_0000333), not an anatomical part.
Narrower: a flower bud of a male flower. Sex is a state of the same bearer, as in 'male flowers' (pattern 04), so no new class is needed.
